# results/paper/ — the paper's result tables and figures

**This is the canonical location for artifacts.** The generation scripts in `tools/` write
here directly. The manuscript directory `paper/` holds only the manuscript itself
(`sections/` / `claims.md` / `outline.md` / `refs.bib`) and keeps no copies of artifacts —
two copies of a table drift apart, so generation and publication share one path.

## Figures and plotting code

The plotting code for the paper's figures is **`code/make_content_figs.py`**. It has three
entry points and produces **5 figures** (`fig_distribution()` alone produces three):

| Artifact | Content | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| `figs/fig_distribution.{pdf,png}` | Data distributions (SBP/DBP on a shared axis + subject-level age) | `--only dist` |
| `figs/fig_dist_bp.{pdf,png}` | Distributions · blood pressure alone | same |
| `figs/fig_dist_age.{pdf,png}` | Distributions · age alone | same |
| `figs/fig_scatter_vital_row.{pdf,png}` | Prediction scatter (one VitalDB row: segment-level SBP/DBP, subject-level age) | `--only scatter` |
| `figs/fig_history_gain.{pdf,png}` | Cumulative history ΔMAE | `--only history` |

(Plus the hand-drawn `fig1_framework.pdf` — 6 PDFs in the directory in total. Only the PDFs
are version-controlled; the PNGs are regenerable and ignored.)

```bash
python results/paper/code/make_content_figs.py            # all three content figures
python results/paper/code/make_content_figs.py --only dist
```

Data sources are **only** `figure_data/*.csv.gz` and the tables in this directory. Styling is
in `code/_paper_style.py`, whose palette is quantitatively validated for color-vision
deficiency by `code/_cvd.py` (four CVD simulations + CIEDE2000; worst pairwise ΔE 17.8 against
a threshold of 15). You can re-verify that claim yourself:

```bash
python results/paper/code/_cvd.py     # exit code 0 = all checks pass
```

### ⚠ Figure 1 is **hand-drawn** and is not generated by any script here

`figs/fig1_framework.pdf` is drawn by the author (exported from a browser/drawio tool). **No
code in this directory generates it, and none is needed.**

To change it: edit the source file, re-export, and overwrite this copy. **Do not attempt to
reproduce it in code.** Because it is not a script product, any "rerun the scripts" or "delete
everything not in the script's output manifest" operation will delete it — exclude it
explicitly.

## Contents

| Subdirectory | Contents | Generator |
|---|---|---|
| `main/` | Main experiment: `main.csv` | `tools/make_paper_tables.py` |
| `ablation/` | The five ablation arms, `ablation.csv` (with Δ columns) | `tools/make_paper_tables.py` |
| `transfer/` | The causal head transplanted into comparison models, `transfer.csv` (with gain columns) | same |
| `history/` | Cumulative history, `history.csv` | same |
| `wearable/` | iwshi_bp wearable-domain transfer, `iwshi_bp.csv` (six arms) | same |
| `analysis/` | Data description: `dataset_stats.csv`, `pretrain_pools.csv`, `subject_level.csv` | `tools/make_data_tables.py` |
| `figure_data/` | The **trimmed derived data** needed to redraw the figures (4.6 MB) | `tools/export_figure_data.py` |
| `code/` | **Plotting code for the three content figures** + style `_paper_style.py` + palette validation `_cvd.py` | — |
| `figs/` | **The paper's figures**: the hand-drawn `fig1_framework.pdf` plus three from `code/` | see above |

> The subdirectory is named `analysis/` rather than `data/` to avoid colliding with the
> top-level `data/` (the training-time data layer).

**Regeneration** (in dependency order):

```bash
python tools/export_figure_data.py            # trimmed plot data (figure_data/)
python tools/make_paper_tables.py             # 5 experiment tables (slow: reads all predictions)
python tools/make_data_tables.py              # 3 data-description tables

python results/paper/code/make_content_figs.py    # figures (reads figure_data/ and the tables above)
```

## Four things to know before reading these tables

### 1. Best seed only, and one seed governs an entire arm

Each arm takes the **best** of its 5 seeds (not the 5-seed mean). Selection criterion = the
arm's **mean MAE over the cells reported in that table**; once chosen, **the same seed is
applied to every cell of that arm** — seeds are not picked per cell, which would amount to
selecting on the data. The selected seed is recorded in each table's `seed` column.

**The cost:** arms use different seeds, so differences between rows are *not* paired
same-seed differences. Under this convention every arm gets its own best case, so the
**measured gaps are a lower bound on the effect of the component in question**. This is an
inherent property of the convention, not an error.

### 2. The ablation table's Δ is computed on the intersection segment set

The `w/o pretraining` arm's stream contains a **different set of segments** from the other four
arms (the main stream was materialized before the cross-source same-name fix). Measured: main
1,704,858 segments / randinit 1,712,483 / **intersection 1,698,983** (99.66% of main). The
whole table is restricted to the intersection; otherwise the randinit row's difference would
mix "different segments" into "different pretraining".

### 3. `transfer.csv` and `main.csv` use the **same** seed

Placed side by side in the paper they do not disagree (the same encoder's `seg_mlp` matches
cell for cell across the two tables). This was not always true: `transfer.csv` used to select
its seed separately by `causal_attn`, which made MMR / PaPaGei-S report two different sets of
numbers in the two tables. **That criterion also carried a selection bias** — picking the seed
that is best at `causal_attn` systematically inflates the gain (MMR's selected seed was the
one with the largest gain, s3 = 0.811, against a 5-seed mean of 0.565).

After removing the bias the gains are no longer uniformly positive: **28 of 30 cells are
positive**; MMR vital/DBP and PaPaGei-S aurora/SBP turn slightly negative (−0.007 / −0.121).
Our own six cells remain clearly positive (+1.16 to +3.73).

### 4. `wearable/iwshi_bp.csv` spans two model generations and includes contaminated arms

Arms ①②③④⑤ use `beatmae_v25c`; ★ uses `beatmae_v25c3`. The two share the same architecture and
recipe in their checkpoint configs and both have 5,952,974 parameters; the only difference is
`data.sources`. Strictly speaking they are still two separate training runs.
**Arms ②④⑤ include iwshi_bp itself, so evaluating them on iwshi_bp is contaminated** — treat
them as controls only.

## Data description (`analysis/`)

### Folds: only the `fold` column counts

**Test folds = 1 and 2** (uniform across the project). The manifest also carries a `split`
column with values `train`/`test`/`val`/`f0`–`f4`/empty, which is **completely orthogonal to
`fold` and must not be used for splitting**:

- `f0`–`f4` total 127,617 segments = the **full iwshi_bp set** (its own 5-fold CV)
- `train`/`test`/`val` total 36,288 segments = the **full Aurora set** (its original dataset split)
- Everything else is empty

Splitting Aurora by `split` gives test = 169 subjects; by `fold` it gives **238** — a
difference of 69 subjects. All experiments use `fold` (`run_meta.json`'s `test_folds` plus
`exclude_folds`/`include_folds` in `train/pretrain.py`).

### Training/test pools (`pretrain_pools.csv`)

| Pool | Composition | Subjects | Segments |
|---|---|---|---|
| Training pool | mimic.train + vital.train + aurora.train | 4,832 | 3,830,393 |
| Test pool | vital.test + aurora.test | 796 | 294,360 |
| Excluded pool | mimic.test (**the whole fold is unused**) | 407 | 660,842 |

### Mean/SD columns — for figure captions, no need to back out of histograms

Every row of `dataset_stats.csv` and `pretrain_pools.csv` carries two groups. **They are at
different aggregation levels and must not be mixed:**

| Columns | Level | Denominator |
|---|---|---|
| `人级年龄均值` / `人级年龄SD` (subject-level age) | take each subject's segment-age median, then average over **subjects** | number of subjects |
| `段级SBP均值` / `段级SBP_SD` / `段级DBP均值` / `段级DBP_SD` (segment-level BP) | computed directly over **segments** | number of BP-labeled segments |

SD is the sample SD (ddof=1) throughout. Measured on the training pool: segment-level SBP
121.5 ± 22.2 / DBP 62.0 ± 13.1; subject-level age 57.8 ± 15.8.

### ⚠ Table segment counts differ from training-log counts by 0.6% (not a protocol disagreement)

The tables report the **structural** count (all `sig_ok=1` segments after the fold split). The
training script applies two further loader-side filters on top: a patch-length pre-screen, and
`val_ds`'s `max_rows`, which **subsamples the whole manifest uniformly first and then filters
by fold** (`data/corpus_dataset.py:119-129`). Training pool 3,830,393 segments → log
`train=3,802,969` (a difference of 27,424). **Use the tables' structural count when describing
the data.**

## Figures

Unified styling lives in `code/_paper_style.py` (Times New Roman + a CVD-validated palette);
change it once and it applies to the whole paper.

### ⚠ The history figure must be plotted from **preds**, not reconstructed from `history.csv`

The same figure has two paths, and they do not agree exactly:

| Path | Precision |
|---|---|
| Read preds directly | **full precision** ← the paper figure should use this |
| Read `history.csv` | gains are stored to 3 decimals, so up to 0.0005 of rounding → 0.67% sub-pixel difference |

Maximum numerical deviation between the two is **0.0005** (the table's rounding), not a
protocol difference. **The sole authority is preds**
(`results/probe/<exp>/full/stream/preds/`).

### ⚠ The distribution figure's display cropping

The histogram binning domain is `[30, 258)` mmHg (**covering all data**), but the **display
range is cropped to `[30, 204]`**, and the amount cropped away is annotated on the figure (the
`outside view:` line).

This is done because numpy's histogram assigns values exactly equal to the last edge to the
final bin; if the last bin edge falls inside the data, that boundary rule actually fires, and a
count-based export **cannot distinguish** 204.0 from 204.5 — the two paths would inevitably
disagree. **The cropping is an explicit choice, not silent data loss.**

## `figure_data/`: letting readers redraw the figures

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `sbp/dbp/age.csv.gz` | Per-segment predictions (`src, sid, y_true, y_pred`), seed=s4, domains=vital+aurora |
| `dist_bp.csv.gz` | SBP/DBP histograms, 1 mmHg × 227 bins of counts |
| `dist_bp_stats.csv` | N/median/extremes, as annotated on the figure |
| `dist_age.csv.gz` | Subject-level age medians (6,081 rows) |

**This is a derived copy. The sole authority remains
`results/probe/<exp>/full/stream/preds/`.** If numbers disagree, preds wins — and rerun
`tools/export_figure_data.py`.

BP is stored as **counts** rather than per-segment values: at 4.8M segments, storing raw values
is 76 MB gzipped, while the distribution figure only needs a histogram. Storing at 1 mmHg
resolution costs 2 KB and lets any coarser binning (e.g. 3 mmHg) be produced by integer
addition — **exactly**, with no loss. Medians and extremes cannot be recovered from counts, so
BP carries a separate statistics file. (Age stores per-subject values, from which the
statistics follow directly, so it needs no companion file.)
